elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM" (unchanged; also only effective "at the end of any calendar month")

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer convenience termination
elements.evidence: "IBM will refund to Customer any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: Redline is silent on any IBM convenience-termination right; no operative language added or removed on that point
"at least one month's prior written notice" — one month is below the 60–90 day band and was not amended

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term
elements.evidence: No inserted language limiting IBM convenience termination to the end of the then-current term

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination requires 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: No inserted 90-day notice requirement applicable to IBM

offending_extra_words: and IBM will refund to Customer any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective date of termination
reasons: The locked fallback level is not completed: the Customer notice period remains "at least one month's prior written notice", short of the 60–90 day fallback band, and nothing was added to confine any IBM convenience termination to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.
Only the fee-cap element of the fallback was delivered ("will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' recurring Charges"); a level is complete only when every atomic element is met.

Minimality fails: the edit imports the preferred-level pro-rata prepaid-fee refund on top of a fallback target, mixing the two bargains, and expands 18 words to 55 (ratio 3.06) where a short operator/number change plus a separate short insertion would suffice.
The one-month notice figure could have been fixed with a two-word numeric change; instead the notice deficiency was left untouched while unrelated protection was appended to limb (b).

Intent is otherwise preserved: the prerequisite-attachment carve-out, end-of-month timing and Attachment A mechanics remain effective and no dangling term is created ("recurring Charges" tracks the existing "Charges" usage).
